about.title: Huntington Park Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and it often happens fast — a single moment on Florence Avenue or State Street, and suddenly you're left with grief and unanswered questions. Huntington Park recorded 3 traffic deaths and 250 injuries in the most recent full year, numbers that represent real families in this Los Angeles County community. California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with other dependents or heirs eligible under certain circumstances. These claims can address funeral and burial expenses, lost financial support, and the loss of a loved one's companionship and guidance. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we're a free service that connects grieving families with an independent attorney who can walk through what happened, who may have standing to file, and what the two-year deadline means for your specific situation. You don't have to sort through this alone.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to specific people, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children. An attorney can help clarify whether you or other relatives qualify as heirs or dependents.

items.title: Awareness of the Filing Deadline
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity involve a much shorter window. Missing that deadline can end your ability to recover, so early guidance matters.

items.title: Clarity on What Losses Count
items.desc: Beyond funeral and burial costs, California law recognizes lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance as recoverable losses. An attorney can explain how these apply to your family's circumstances.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none of those exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing under certain conditions. An independent attorney can review your family's situation to explain who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in Huntington Park?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to bring a wrongful death claim. If the crash involved a government vehicle or roadway defect, the deadline to act can be much shorter. Because Huntington Park sees regular traffic on corridors like Gage and Florence Avenue, getting timely guidance matters.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case?
items.answer: No, they are separate. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action seeking compensation for the family's losses. Both can happen at the same time without affecting each other's outcome.
